record.paper_title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems
record.context_brief: Approximation scheme compact support of second branch
record.original_question: For the same approximating problem -Δu + u^q/(u+ε)^(q+α) = λu^p in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, where ε > 0 and 0 < q < p, the cited work produces a second critical point v_ε converging as ε → 0 to a nonnegative solution v. Does the limit solution v have compact support?

evidence.quote: Then he proves that this functional has a minimum u_ε ≥ 0 and also a second critical point v_ε ≥ 0 ... and that when ε goes to 0 they tend to ... solutions u ≥ 0 and v ≥ 0.
One can guess that u > 0 and that maybe v has compact support, but this is not proved in the paper.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a smooth bounded domain, and fix real numbers $\alpha > 0$, $\lambda > 0$, and exponents $0 < q < p$ with $p$ subcritical (i.e. $p < (N+2)/(N-2)$ if $N \geq 3$). For each $\varepsilon > 0$ consider the approximating semilinear elliptic problem
$$
-\Delta u + \frac{u^{q}}{(u+\varepsilon)^{q+\alpha}} = \lambda u^{p} \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial\Omega,
$$
sought among nonnegative functions. The associated energy functional admits (for $\lambda$ in an appropriate range) a nonnegative minimizer $u_\varepsilon \geq 0$ and a second nonnegative critical point $v_\varepsilon \geq 0$ of mountain-pass type. Assume that as $\varepsilon \to 0^{+}$ one has $u_\varepsilon \to u$ and $v_\varepsilon \to v$ in a suitable sense, where $u, v \geq 0$ are nonnegative solutions of the limit singular problem
$$
-\Delta w + \frac{1}{w^{\alpha}}\,\chi_{\{w>0\}} = \lambda w^{p} \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad w = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial\Omega.
$$
Question: Does the limit second solution $v$ have compact support in $\Omega$ (i.e. is the set $\{x \in \Omega : v(x) > 0\}$ compactly contained in $\Omega$, equivalently does $v$ exhibit a free boundary inside $\Omega$)?
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this specific question (whether the second mountain-pass branch limit solution $v$ has compact support) was located. The question is posed as an open problem in the surveyed literature on singular nonlinear elliptic equations with absorption, and no subsequent work confirming or refuting compact support of $v$ was identified.

status_evidence.title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems regarding free boundary / compact support of solutions to singular elliptic equations with absorption.
status_evidence.claim: The compact support property of the limit second critical point v is explicitly stated as not proved.
